evidence.note: Read run_tests.sh and /opt/score_golden.py to learn how scoring works and how the harness communicates with the LSP over stdio — direct match to the anchor-5 'read run_tests to learn scoring' behavior.

Used Python with collections.Counter to enumerate distinct $method types AND their frequencies (12 methods, ~68K cases); derived the initialize handshake, Content-Length framing, and the didOpen-empty-text/read-from-disk quirk — method-frequency mapping is an anchor-8 element.
Inspected representative Java files across categories (simple/algorithms/oop/jdk/errors) and studied golden.jsonl response shapes for specific methods before starting to build.

Exact response schemas were largely discovered via test failures rather than anticipated: documentSymbol range (124), hover field format (130), selectionRange parent direction (135/145), and semantic-token legend decoded from golden data only after 0% pass (151) — reactive discovery, not the upfront spec-driven model of anchor 8.
Continued probing during build by sending a manual Content-Length JSON-RPC request to diff actual vs golden output — self-correcting probing above a plain 5, but still reactive.

reasoning: The opening orientation was systematic and above the anchor-5 floor: the agent read the scorer and harness, enumerated every method and its frequency via Counter, studied representative response shapes, and correctly derived the handshake plus the didOpen/read-from-disk quirk before coding (steps 3-9). It falls short of 8 because exact per-method schemas and JDT-LS conventions (documentSymbol/hover/selectionRange/semantic-token legend) were mostly discovered reactively through 0% test failures rather than anticipated, and position/encoding conventions and the LSP spec were never systematically cross-referenced. The sustained-but-reactive probing during building places it at a 6.
